title: Britain’s longest place name was reportedly invented in 1869 as a publicity stunt

cover.alt: The long platform sign at Llanfairpwllgwyngyll railway station on Anglesey, spelling out the village’s 58-character name.

body: Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwllllantysiliogogogoch, a village on Anglesey in north Wales, has a name of 58 characters, meaning roughly ‘St Mary’s church in the hollow of the white hazels near the fierce whirlpool and St Tysilio’s church of the red cave’. The long form was supposedly contrived in 1869 as an early publicity stunt, to give the village the longest railway station name in Britain; a local tailor is credited, though who really did it, and exactly when, is less certain. About 2,900 people live there, most of whom call the place Llanfairpwll, and the station sign is the main attraction.

slides.question: How many syllables are in the full 58-character name?
slides.explanation: Eighteen syllables in 58 characters, or 51 letters counted the Welsh way, where ‘ch’ and ‘ll’ are single letters.

slides.label: characters, or 51 letters the Welsh way, where ch and ll count as one letter
slides.text: The station sign gives English speakers an approximate pronunciation. Locals shorten the name to Llanfairpwll or Llanfair PG.

slides.heading: Characters in the name
slides.note: The community’s official name is the 20-character Llanfairpwllgwyngyll

slides.heading: Match the Welsh to its meaning
slides.explanation: Llanfair pwll gwyn gyll: St Mary’s church of the pool of the white hazels; chwyrn drobwll: fierce whirlpool; gogof goch: red cave.

slides.heading: Who did it?
slides.text: The Welsh scholar Sir John Morris-Jones said the name was created by a local tailor whose name he did not confide, letting the secret die with him. The true originator and date are less certain. What is certain is that the stunt worked: the station and its sign are the village’s most popular attraction.

left.label: Claim
left.text: The longest place name in Europe and the second-longest one-word place name in the world.

right.label: Reality
right.text: It is a 19th-century invention, and the community’s official name is the much shorter Llanfairpwllgwyngyll.
